operatorEvidence.name: Darlington New Nuclear Project — Unit 1
operatorEvidence.facts: OPG reports that Unit 1 reactor-building construction is progressing above its completed basemat in summer 2026, after CNSC clearance of the foundation hold point. This collection includes the first 300 MW BWRX-300 unit under construction. Three additional units remain subject to regulatory approvals and are excluded; the proposed 1,200 MW four-unit fleet is not the included construction capacity. An operating licence is still required before commissioning/operation.

operatorEvidence.name: Palisades — existing-reactor refurbishment and commissioning
operatorEvidence.facts: Holtec reports completed major refurbishment work and ongoing testing, restoration, fuel-loading-related activities and preparations for startup at the existing Palisades reactor. It confirms reconnection to the 345-kV switchyard on September 11, 2026 after extensive restoration. That connection is not confirmation of commercial nuclear generation. This collection includes the physical existing-reactor restart work; the separate proposed Pioneer SMR-300 reactors are excluded.

name: Rabbit’s Foot Solar — Bowie County, Texas

geocoding.precision: locality/county; exact project parcel not verified

facts: RWE’s June 11, 2026 release describes Rabbit’s Foot as a 298 MWac solar project in Bowie County. Onsite construction began earlier in 2026, Meta signed a long-term power-purchase agreement, and commercial operation is targeted by the end of 2027. This is a planned generation rating, not delivered power.

name: T.H. Wharton new gas peaker units — Houston

geocoding.precision: reported existing plant point; not a verified new-unit entrance

facts: NRG confirms its two new simple-cycle gas units at T.H. Wharton reached commercial operation May 26, 2026. The operator article describes a combined 456 MW nameplate rating; its quarterly results use a 415 MW project figure. These are different published ratings, not two separate additions. Older Wharton units are excluded from the new-project capacity.
